assertions.assertion: Problem statement names what decides the right payment (litres with unit converted, at co-op rate; month by dairy local time) and says paid/stated amount can differ, checkable per pickup or farm-month
assertions.evidence: Hypothesis: "each pickup should be paid by its litres (converted from gallons if needed) and counted in the month it happened at the dairy (UTC-7). The code can give a different number." It does not state the rate, but "paid by its litres" covers the per-litre rule in general terms. It can be checked one pickup or one farm-month at a time.

assertions.assertion: Problem statement does not build in a cause or fix
assertions.evidence: The hypothesis states the correct rules (litres after any gallon conversion, and the month at the dairy, identified as UTC-7). It does not say how the code goes wrong. Causes such as "ignores the unit column" and "takes the first 7 characters of the UTC time" appear only in the Findings, as evidence.

assertions.assertion: Both complaints fit the statement and the statement can fail
assertions.evidence: F-07's complaint is a unit conversion problem and F-12's is a month assignment problem; both fit the litres-and-local-month statement. The agent gives a falsifier: "It would be false if every payout and statement matched the README rules."
